abstract.t: A profile of RFC 5869 for nish/crypto/hkdf: HKDF instantiated with SHA-256, so HashLen is 32. Every requirement quotes RFC 5869, the main source; every binding sentence of RFC 5869 (MUST, MUST NOT, SHALL, SHALL NOT, REQUIRED) is tested or excluded here.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.
nish/crypto/hkdf exports HKDF-Extract and HKDF-Expand for SHA-256. The properties compare them with nish/crypto/hmac, the HMAC-SHA-256 they are built on.

section.name: Interface
Extract
section.sourcecode: // P-EXTRACT-IS-HMAC covers R-EXTRACT — HKDF-Extract is HMAC-SHA-256 keyed by the salt forall (salt: u8[] /* 1..150 */, ikm: u8[] /* 0..150 */) => hkdfExtractSha256(salt, ikm) === hmacSha256(salt, ikm)

blockquote.t: if not provided, it is set to a string of HashLen zeros.

section.sourcecode: // P-EMPTY-SALT covers R-SALT — an absent salt is HashLen zero octets forall (ikm: u8[] /* 0..150 */) => hkdfExtractSha256([], ikm) === hmacSha256(zeros(32), ikm)

blockquote.t: PRK a pseudorandom key (of HashLen octets)

section.sourcecode: // P-PRK-LEN covers R-PRK-LEN — the PRK is HashLen octets forall (salt: u8[] /* 0..150 */, ikm: u8[] /* 0..150 */) => hkdfExtractSha256(salt, ikm).length === 32

section.name: Expand

blockquote.t: L length of output keying material in octets (<= 255*HashLen)

section.t: Note: The RFC states the bound; refusing a longer L with null is how nish/crypto/hkdf honours it.

blockquote.t: info optional context and application specific information (can be a zero-length string)
OKM output keying material (of L octets)

section.sourcecode: // P-EXPAND-LENGTH covers R-L, R-OKM-LEN — Expand gives exactly L octets for L <= 255*HashLen and refuses a longer L forall (prk: u8[] /* 32..64 */, info: u8[] /* 0..40 */, n: i32 /* 0..8300 */) => implies(n <= 255 * 32, hkdfExpandSha256(prk, info, n) !== null && unwrap(hkdfExpandSha256(prk, info, n)).length === n) && implies(n > 255 * 32, hkdfExpandSha256(prk, info, n) === null)

blockquote.t: OKM = first L octets of T
T(0) = empty string (zero length) T(1) = HMAC-Hash(PRK, T(0) | info | 0x01) T(2) = HMAC-Hash(PRK, T(1) | info | 0x02)

section.sourcecode: // P-T1-T2 covers R-T — the first two blocks are T(1) and T(2) as §2.3 defines them forall (prk: u8[] /* 32..64 */, info: u8[] /* 0..100 */) => unwrap(hkdfExpandSha256(prk, info, 64)).slice(0, 32) === hmacSha256(prk, info.concat([01])) && unwrap(hkdfExpandSha256(prk, info, 64)).slice(32, 64) === hmacSha256(prk, hmacSha256(prk, info.concat([01])).concat(info).concat([02]))

section.name: Out of Scope
section.t: This contract tests only hkdfExtractSha256 and hkdfExpandSha256; every other export of nish/crypto/hkdf is declared out of scope below, with the reason it is not tested.
Out of scope: hkdfExtractSha384, HKDF over SHA-384 (HashLen 48); RFC 5869 Appendix A has no SHA-384 test case, and this profile fixes the hash to SHA-256
Out of scope: hkdfExpandSha384, HKDF over SHA-384 (HashLen 48); RFC 5869 Appendix A has no SHA-384 test case, and this profile fixes the hash to SHA-256

Out of scope: hkdfExtractSha256Secret, the same derivation taking and giving Secret<u8[]>; what it adds is wiping, a non-functional property this profile cannot observe, covered by tests/wipes/crypto.js, and no test in this contract checks that its output equals the plain function's

Out of scope: hkdfExtractSha384Secret, the same derivation taking and giving Secret<u8[]>; what it adds is wiping, a non-functional property this profile cannot observe, covered by tests/wipes/crypto.js, and no test in this contract checks that its output equals the plain function's

Out of scope: hkdfExpandSha256Secret, the same derivation taking and giving Secret<u8[]>; what it adds is wiping, a non-functional property this profile cannot observe, covered by tests/wipes/crypto.js, and no test in this contract checks that its output equals the plain function's

Out of scope: hkdfExpandSha384Secret, the same derivation taking and giving Secret<u8[]>; what it adds is wiping, a non-functional property this profile cannot observe, covered by tests/wipes/crypto.js, and no test in this contract checks that its output equals the plain function's

Out of scope: hkdfSha256Secret, the same derivation taking and giving Secret<u8[]>; what it adds is wiping, a non-functional property this profile cannot observe, covered by tests/wipes/crypto.js, and no test in this contract checks that its output equals the plain function's

Out of scope: hkdfSha384Secret, the same derivation taking and giving Secret<u8[]>; what it adds is wiping, a non-functional property this profile cannot observe, covered by tests/wipes/crypto.js, and no test in this contract checks that its output equals the plain function's
Out of scope: hkdfExpandLabelSha256, TLS 1.3's HKDF-Expand-Label (RFC 8446 Section 7.1), not a construction of RFC 5869
Out of scope: hkdfExpandLabelSha384, TLS 1.3's HKDF-Expand-Label (RFC 8446 Section 7.1), not a construction of RFC 5869
Out of scope: hkdfExpandLabelSha256Secret, TLS 1.3's HKDF-Expand-Label (RFC 8446 Section 7.1), not a construction of RFC 5869
Out of scope: hkdfExpandLabelSha384Secret, TLS 1.3's HKDF-Expand-Label (RFC 8446 Section 7.1), not a construction of RFC 5869
Out of scope: hkdfExtractInto, an allocation-free variant writing into caller buffers through an HkdfScratch; its signature takes a class and output offsets, which a ts-interface block cannot declare
Out of scope: hkdfExpandInto, an allocation-free variant writing into caller buffers through an HkdfScratch; its signature takes a class and output offsets, which a ts-interface block cannot declare

Out of scope: hkdfExpandLabelInto, an allocation-free variant writing into caller buffers through an HkdfScratch; its signature takes a class and output offsets, which a ts-interface block cannot declare
Out of scope: hkdfExpandLabelSha256Held, Expand-Label of a held Secret PRK, written in place into a Secret or a caller buffer; likewise RFC 8446, not RFC 5869
Out of scope: hkdfExpandLabelSha384Held, Expand-Label of a held Secret PRK, written in place into a Secret or a caller buffer; likewise RFC 8446, not RFC 5869
Out of scope: hkdfExpandLabelHeldInto, Expand-Label of a held Secret PRK, written in place into a Secret or a caller buffer; likewise RFC 8446, not RFC 5869
Out of scope: HkdfScratch, a class holding reusable buffers, not a function; the profile declares functions only

abstract.t: This document specifies a simple Hashed Message Authentication Code (HMAC)-based key derivation function (HKDF), which can be used as a building block in various protocols and applications. The key derivation function (KDF) is intended to support a wide range of applications and requirements, and is conservative in its use of cryptographic hash functions. This document is not an Internet Standards Track specification; it is published for informational purposes.

front.title: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels

abstract.t: In many standards track documents several words are used to signify the requirements in the specification. These words are often capitalized. This document defines these words as they should be interpreted in IETF documents. This document specifies an Internet Best Current Practices for the Internet Community, and requests discussion and suggestions for improvements.

front.title: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words

abstract.t: RFC 2119 specifies common key words that may be used in protocol specifications. This document aims to reduce the ambiguity by clarifying that only UPPERCASE usage of the key words have the defined special meanings.
